newsitem.title: SWEDEN: AGA says aims for 15 pct operating margin.
newsitem.headline: AGA says aims for 15 pct operating margin.

text.p: Swedish medical and industrial gas maker AGA AB said on Monday it aimed to reach an operating margin of 15 percent in 1999 at the latest for a return on equity of about 15 percent.
The company said in a statement that restructuring would lower its costs in the second half of 1997 and they would have a full effect of savings of around 200 million crowns ($26.5 million) in 1998.
The company posted a 17 percent fall in profit after financial items, excluding capital gains, to 1.76 billion crowns in 1996.
The profit was somewhat lower than expected with analysts in a Reuter poll targeting a profit of 1.81 billion crowns excluding capital gains.

Including the 1.79 billion crowns in a capital gain from the sale of shares in power company Gullspangs Kraft, pre-tax profit rose 31 percent to 3.55 billion crowns last year. In 1995, capital gains amounted to 601 million crowns.
Sales fell three percent to 12.86 billion crowns, but excluding the effect of changed exchange rates, sales rose by four percent, the company said.
"We are not satisfied with the 1996 result," AGA chief executive officer Lennart Selander said in a statement.
"It is true that we continued to increase our market shares, but the sales trend was weak and could not compensate for a substantial rise in costs."
Selander, which took over as CEO on January 1, 1997, said he set some key objectives for the company.
"AGA shall grow somewhat faster than the market for industrial and medical gases," he said.
"AGA shall achieve a 15 percent operating margin by 1999 at the latest. AGA shall have a return on equity of approximately 15 percent. AGA shall increase its earnings per share every year."
In 1996 AGA's earnings per share excluding capital gains fell to 5.11 crowns from 6.31 crowns after tax. The company proposed that the dividend would remain at 2.70 crowns a share.
"In order to achieve these goals, our operations must be made more effective," Selander said.
"An extensive restructuring programme has therefore been started. This will lead to a reduction of central costs and will also affect our subsidiaries."

Restructuring and rationalization in connection with the introduction of a new organisation will entail non-recurring costs of more than 100 million crowns, which will be charged to earnings in the first quarter of 1997, Selander said.
Most of the costs are related to the reduction in the number of employees, he said.
"This rationalisation programme will reduce our costs in the second half of 1997 and the full impact, about 200 million crowns, will occur in 1998."
Regarding market trends, Selander forecast a continued strong growth for liquid gases, while he saw the volume trend for cylinder gases remaining weak in AGA's key markets.
"As new plants go on stream, we will be able to solve supply problems in several of our markets," Selander said.
He said economic trends varied.
"AGA has further strengthened its position in the U.S., where a positive economic trend continues," he said.
"The major part of our operations, however, are located in Europe where we have so far seen little sign of an improved business climate.
"The situation in Latin America in less uniform. Some economies are showing strong growth while others are undergoing a recession."
-- Birgitta Forsberg, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1006
